title: On Zion, His Most Holy Mount
description: On Zion, His Most Holy Mount in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 290 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Gospel Feast”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: On Zi-on, his most ho-ly mount, God will a feast pre-pare; And Is-rael's sons, and Gen-tile lands, Shall in the ban-quet share.

lines: On Zion, his most holy mount,
And Israel's sons, and Gentile lands,
See to the vilest of the vile
Sit with the heirs of heaven!
The pained, the sick, the dying, now
But, O, what draughts of bliss unknown,
When, with the myriads round the throne,
We join the feast of heaven!
And springs of life, that never dry,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
